input.quote: (a) This Agreement is governed in all respects by the laws of the State of Delaware without giving effect to its conflict of laws principles. Each Party hereby irrevocably submits for all disputes to the exclusive jurisdiction and venue of the state and federal courts located in New York, New York.
input.rationale: Section 14(a) picks Delaware law but sends all disputes to the New York courts, so the forum is not the "corresponding" Delaware court required by the fallback; more materially, Section 8 mandates that any controversy "shall be settled by arbitration administered by the American Arbitration Association", which displaces the court forum entirely and contradicts the exclusive-jurisdiction submission in 14(a). A mandatory arbitration mechanic instead of courts fails both checklist levels, so we moved the clause to the preferred position: New York law with the state and federal courts in New York County as the exclusive merits forum, and conformed Section 8 (including its heading) to that venue while leaving the jury waiver and one-year limitation untouched. The prevailing-party clause in 14(d) still mentions arbitration costs, but it is conditional recovery language rather than an arbitration mandate, so we left it alone.

proposal.summary: New York governing law; exclusive New York County courts; remove mandatory AAA arbitration
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We moved governing law to New York and confirmed the state and federal courts in New York County as the exclusive merits forum, replacing the mandatory AAA arbitration mechanic that conflicted with that venue. Delaware or California law with the matching courts is our fallback if New York law is not acceptable.

ops.oldText: Any controversy or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement, or the breach thereof, shall be settled by arbitration administered by the American Arbitration Association under its Commercial Arbitration Rules, and judgment on the award rendered by the arbitrator(s) may be entered in any court having jurisdiction thereof
ops.newText: Any controversy or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement, or the breach thereof, shall be resolved exclusively in the courts specified in Section 14(a)

ops.oldText: the laws of the State of Delaware
ops.newText: the laws of the State of New York

ops.oldText: state and federal courts located in New York, New York
ops.newText: state and federal courts located in New York County, New York
